problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x,0,yz⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=y-{x}^{2}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨z,0,0⟩,\,∇f=⟨-2x,1,0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,2,-1).$
worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2x & 1 & 0 \\ x & 0 & yz\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1(yz)-0(0)]i-[-2x(yz)-0(x)]j+[-2x(0)-1(x)]k \\  & =yz\,i+2xyz\,j-x\,k \\  & =⟨yz,2xyz,-x⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(y-{x}^{2})⟨z,0,0⟩+⟨yz,2xyz,-x⟩ \\  & =⟨z(y-{x}^{2}),0,0⟩+⟨yz,2xyz,-x⟩ \\  & =⟨z(2y-{x}^{2}),2xyz,-x⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(0,2,-1) & =⟨(-1)(2(2)-(0)^{2}),2(0)(2)(-1),-0⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
